(`GET /v1/accounts/{account}/recovery-mechanisms`; `AC-A5.3`).

For a passkey (`F-028`): its assertion, whose challenge is that same 32-byte
`reclaim_challenge`. Ingress verifies it.

proof_credential.description:
The credential that proves it works: an active member of the holder's set covering the
account.

signature.description:
For a `key` credential: its signature, 64 bytes of hex, over the challenge that binds the
account and its custody epoch, as the custody view shows it
(`ledger_core::custody::reclaim_challenge`).

RecoveryMechanismsBody.description:
The recovery mechanisms that apply, and the digest a command that makes an account owned
carries as its acknowledgement (`REQ-AU-9`, `AC-A5.3`).

RedeemBody.description: `redeem` (SPEC §8.1): value leaves the book to the issuance counterparty.

amount.description: Minor units, as a decimal-integer string.

reference.description:

wherever its operation is read and never read by aledgent. Part of the request: a repeat
under the same client key with a different one is `ERR-ClientKeyReused`.

Refusal.description: A refusal names one condition of the closed list (REQ-CS-4, REQ-ER-1). It is always a 4xx, never a success body carrying an error.

RegisterAliasBody.description:
`register_alias` (`REQ-RC-7`, amendment 0024): name the account in the path by (source, name),
as a seed's aliases do. A system account's role is one (`ops/runbooks/system-accounts.md`).

name.description:
The name within the source: a role (`issuer/fee`) or a prior system's identifier. At most
256 bytes; never personal data (`INV-17`).

source.description:
The source: 16 bytes as 32 hex digits, or a name of at most 16 ASCII bytes, zero-padded
(`system-role` for a system account's role, as the migration's role aliases).

RegisterAssetBody.description:
`register_asset` (`REQ-AS-2`, `F-013`): an asset, registered book-only (amendment 0011,
`REQ-AS-7`), with its one precision.

review.description: The reviewed change it comes from, 32 bytes of hex.

RegisterCredentialBody.description: `register_credential` (SPEC §8.1, `REQ-AU-20`, `F-012`): a new member of the caller's own set.

scope.description:
The accounts it is limited to; absent for all of the identity's. Within the presenting
credential's own scope (`REQ-AU-4`).

verifier.description: Its verifier: public material, hex. A key that can sign a reclaim proof is 32 bytes.

RegisterCredentialRequest.description:
`POST /v1/credentials` as a caller sends it (`F-028`): a credential of any scheme. Ingress turns
it into the [`RegisterCredentialBody`] the core receives, which holds only public material.

- `key` (the default): `verifier` is the 32-byte public key, hex.
- `webauthn-es256`: `passkey` carries the browser's registration, made over a challenge from
  `POST /v1/auth/challenge` with purpose `register`. Ingress verifies it.
- `api-key`: nothing else. Ingress draws the secret, keeps its hash, and returns the key once,
  in `api_key` of the reply.

scope.description:
The accounts it is limited to; absent for all of the identity's (`REQ-AU-20`), within the
presenting credential's own scope (`REQ-AU-4`).

RegisterIntegratingPartyBody.description:
`register_integrating_party` on the operator surface (`REQ-ID-7`, amendment 0011): the
operator's policy authority alone.

principals.description: The principals tied to it on registration, each tied to no party. May be empty.

layer.description: Every position the layer holds in the range.

to.description: The first position after the range.

missing.description: Positions the layer holds that were never ingested.

unknown.description: Final coordinates the core holds that the layer no longer shows.

RescheduleUpgradeBody.description:
`reschedule_upgrade` (`REQ-RT-20`, `T-037-15`): move the scheduled upgrade to input `from`, later
than the command's own.

from.description: The input number the upgrade now applies from.

ReserveBody.description:
`reserve` (SPEC §8.1, `REQ-BA-4`): acknowledged at `Received`; the decision follows by query and
notification (`REQ-CS-3`).

amount.description: Minor units, as a decimal-integer string.

deadline.description: The operation's deadline; the deployment's default for reservations if absent.

payer.description: The account the value is reserved against.

reference.description:
Pass-through data (`REQ-PO-5`): one JSON value of at most 1 KiB, the caller's own, echoed
wherever its operation is read and never read by aledgent. Part of the request: a repeat
under the same client key with a different one is `ERR-ClientKeyReused`.

ResolutionBody.description:
What a `Needs-Review` operation resolves to: `Settled` or `Released` only (amendment 0006
items 1 and 4). Value to return after that is a reversal operation.

oneOf.description: `Settled`.
`Released`.

ResolutionEvidenceBody.description: The evidence a resolution cites. Exactly one field.

oneOf.description: A record the settlement store ingested.
Non-inclusion of the operation's instruction under the last finalised head.

No mechanical proof (`REQ-RC-5`, step 3): only after the settlement adapter checked
submitted evidence and found none, and only with a second, distinct principal agreeing.

ResolveBody.description: `resolve_operation` of the operation in the path (`REQ-OS-2`, `F-013`).

ScheduledUpgradeBody.description: An upgrade the writer has scheduled (`T-037-23`).

from.description: The input number it applies from: that input and those after it run under the new code.

SessionReply.description: A session (`F-028`): present `session` as a bearer token until `expires_at`. It is a secret.

credential.description: The passkey it signed in with.

SettlementCallBody.description: What a call does on the settlement layer (`F-027`, `DEC-18`).

oneOf.description: Pay out a reservation.

amount.description: The exact amount: minor units, as a decimal-integer string.

oneOf.description: Store an anchor: a number and 32 bytes.

Bind a book-only asset (amendment 0011, `REQ-AS-8`): the layer records its holding of the
asset at `location` as the deployment's position only if it equals `amount` exactly.

amount.description: The book's outstanding balance: minor units, as a decimal-integer string. May be zero.

location.description: Its location on the layer, in the layer's textual form (`Here(100)`).

anchor.description: Where an anchor's checkpoint stands: `pending`, `submitted` or `final` (`F-017`).

attestation.description: What the core made of an attestation (`DEC-20`).

condition.description: A condition a check detected on the way (`ERR-AmountMismatch`).

SignalsBody.description:
The operational signals (`F-018`, `NFR-11`): counts, ages and times, never a ledger fact.
The operator's, with the `read_signals` operator kind. Ages are in milliseconds at the time
of the read.

anchor_in_flight_age.description: How long the checkpoint in flight has waited for finality, if one is.

anchor_incidents.description:
Anchoring's incidents, per kind (`commitment_mismatch`, `unknown_anchor`,
`position_difference`); `latest` is not known for them and is zero.

anchor_lag.description:
Anchor lag (`F-017`): time since the newest `Final` checkpoint was created; before the
first is final, the age of the oldest checkpoint; absent while there is none.

audit.description: The audit trail's shipping (`T-013-13`); absent when the core ships to no audit store.

book.description:
The book's size (`T-018-11`): what `T-036-17`'s disk-backed store is required by. Absent
from a core that does not count it.

code_source_mismatches.description:
Answers the core host's code fetcher discarded because the bytes were not what their digest
and length name (`T-037-06`, `aledgent_code_source_mismatch_total`), per place it asked: the
cache and each configured source, each listed even at zero. Empty when the node has no
source of code, and from a core with none (the in-process core).

completion_p50.description:
Completion of commands at p50 and p99, in milliseconds, over ingress's latest samples
(`NFR-15`, amendment 0007); absent before the first. Ingress's own, added by the surface.

completion_p99.description: See `completion_p50`. `F-018` pages when it passes the 30 s ceiling.

core_halted.description:
Whether the core has stopped deciding: halted on an input the Agent cannot apply (finding
F18 of `F-032`), or stopped on an incident. Reads go on; every input waits `Received`.

incidents.description: Incidents on the operator channel, per kind.

oldest_open_age.description: The age of the oldest non-terminal operation (`REQ-OP-8`); absent when none is open.

oldest_undecided_age.description:
The age of the oldest row ingress holds undecided — logged, not yet decided by the core
(`REQ-CS-7`); absent when every row is decided. Ingress's own, added by the surface.

oldest_undelivered_age.description: The age of the oldest undelivered notification; absent when none is owed.

review_most_overdue.description: How far past its service level the most overdue entry is.

review_overdue.description: Of which past their service level.

settlement_comparison_age.description: The age of the latest settlement comparison.

settlement_differing.description: Assets whose latest settlement comparison differs (`REQ-PR-5`).

tick_age.description: The age of the last tick the core applied (`DEC-6`, `RISK-7`); absent before the first.

vos_unacknowledged.description:
The core Agent's runtime: Authority decisions (receipts) issued whose invocation is not
acknowledged yet. The runtime refuses more past 256. Absent for the in-process core.

writer_code.description:
The code the core's writer runs (`T-037-23`, `REQ-RT-16`, `REQ-RT-20`, `NFR-11`): the
version in force, its generation, and the upgrade scheduled, as of the last input that
committed. Absent from a core that does not report it (the in-process core, an older core
host): a reader that does not know the field ignores it, and a body without it reads as
"not reported".

writer_fenced_age.description:
How long the core's writer has been fenced, in milliseconds (`T-037-15`, `REQ-RT-20`,
`NFR-11`): since the fence first refused an input that has not committed since, because the
code installed is not the code the writer's state names. Absent while it is not fenced, and
from a core with no fence (the in-process core).

SigningBody.description:
`ack_instruction`, after the acknowledgement: what the adapter did about signing the
instruction (the owner's ruling of 2026-09-24).

instruction.description: The instruction's digest, 32 bytes of hex.

SigningRecordBody.description: What the adapter did about signing an instruction (the owner's ruling of 2026-09-24).

oneOf.description: The one transaction it signed for the instruction, recorded before it submits it.

key.description: The signing key's account on the settlement layer, 32 bytes of hex.

last_valid.description: The last settlement-layer height the transaction can be included at.

nonce.description: The account nonce the transaction carries.

oneOf.description: It will never sign one: the instruction can no longer be signed within its expiry.

StateClassBody.description: The class of a state (`REQ-OP-7`): whether it is final, and whether anything has returned.

oneOf.description: Terminal: the outcome is final.
Not terminal and not refunding: nothing has returned yet.
`Needs-Review`: waiting for a human. Not terminal and not refunding.

closed.description: Whether the period is closed: no posting can still enter it.

from_seq.description: The first posting of the period.

SubjectBody.description: What a grant is over. Exactly one field is present.

oneOf.description: One ledger account.
Every account in delegated custody at the moment of evaluation.
One asset.

One identity, `did:`-shaped (amendment 0025): a delegated grant to open the accounts it
will own.

SubmitEvidenceBody.description:
`submit_evidence` for the operation in the path (`REQ-RC-5`, step 2): where on the settlement
layer the proof of its outcome is, for the settlement adapter to fetch and verify.

transaction.description: The transaction's hash in it, 32 bytes of hex.

SubmitOutboundBody.description: `submit_outbound` of the reserved outbound leg in the path (SPEC §8.1, `REQ-SO-2`).

TiePrincipalBody.description:
`tie_principal` to the party in the path (`REQ-ID-7`, amendment 0011): from then on the
principal's client keys are the party's (`REQ-OP-10`).

TransferBody.description: `transfer` (SPEC §8.1): one leg or many, all or nothing (`US-B1`, `US-B3`).

deadline.description: The operation's deadline; the deployment's default for transfers if absent.

legs.description: The legs, in the order they apply.

reference.description:
Pass-through data (`REQ-PO-5`): one JSON value of at most 1 KiB, the caller's own, echoed
wherever its operation is read and never read by aledgent. Part of the request: a repeat
under the same client key with a different one is `ERR-ClientKeyReused`.

accounts.description: How many kernel accounts the commitment check summed.

rows.description: The check on openings, per asset.

unbalanced.description: Every (currency, layer) that does not sum to zero. Empty when the book balances.

view.description: The view it was read at.

TrialRowBody.description: One asset's trial balance on openings.

openings.description: The signed sum of openings, minor units: zero when it balances.

UnbalancedBody.description: One unbalanced (currency, layer) of the commitment check.

UndeliveredBody.description: An undelivered notification, with its age (`REQ-EV-6`).

age.description: How long it has been owed, in milliseconds.

recipient.description: The principal it is owed to.

UpgradeBody.description:
`upgrade` (`REQ-RT-16`, `T-037-04`): the writer's code becomes the code version `code` from input
`from`. The execution node fetches the version's manifest and artefacts and checks them
(`REQ-RT-17`, `REQ-RT-20`) before the command is logged; the writer decides it under the
upgrade-authority mode in force (`REQ-RT-18`).

code.description: The code version: the `blake2b-256` of its manifest, as 64 hex digits.

from.description: The input number it applies from: later than the command's own.

VenueBody.description: Where an anchor lives on the settlement layer (`F-027` T-027-04).

oneOf.description: The settlement pallet, under an instance.
The settlement contract.

account.description: The contract's account, 32 bytes of hex.

VerdictBody.description: The core's verdict on a submission (`REQ-SI-5`).

oneOf.description: Taken as evidence; the operation's state is the reply's.
Stored; no transition.
The coordinate was seen before (`ERR-ObservationDuplicate` on the refusal path).
It relates to nothing aledgent holds (`ERR-ObservationUnassociated` on the refusal path).

report.description: The report, as the offline verifier prints it.

VerifierBody.description: One credential of an import (`REQ-MG-7`, amendment 0010, `F-028`).

scope.description: The accounts it is limited to; absent for all of the identity's.

verifier.description: The verifier: public material only, hex-encoded.

limit.description: The most that may move in one window, in minor units.

WithdrawBody.description: `withdraw` (SPEC §8.1, `F-010`): an outbound leg, reserved against the payer first.

amount.description: Minor units, as a decimal-integer string.

deadline.description: The operation's deadline; the deployment's default if absent.

reference.description:
Pass-through data (`REQ-PO-5`): one JSON value of at most 1 KiB, the caller's own, echoed
wherever its operation is read and never read by aledgent. Part of the request: a repeat
under the same client key with a different one is `ERR-ClientKeyReused`.

WriterCodeBody.description:
The code the core's writer runs, as the signals carry it (`T-037-23`): what to look at to know
which program is deciding, before and after a switch.

code.description:
The code version in force: the digest of its manifest, 64 hex characters in lower case. All
zeros for a book founded without a named code version (tests).

generation.description: The code generation in force: 0 at genesis, one more after each upgrade.

info.description: The command and query surfaces of aledgent (CTR-CMD, CTR-QRY) and its notifications (CTR-EVT). Amounts are decimal-integer strings of minor units. Identifiers are did:aledgent strings. Times are milliseconds since the Unix epoch. Every route requires a bearer credential, except the two under /v1/auth, which check what their body carries (F-028).

get.description:
Lists the entries made against a subject's accounts, oldest first, one page at a time. Name
exactly one subject: `account` or `identity`. Naming both, or neither, is refused as
`ERR-QueryUnbounded`. `limit` is required, from 1 to 1000; a
request without it, or past it, is refused the same way. `from` and `to` come together, in
milliseconds since the Unix epoch: `from` is inclusive and `to` is exclusive, and `from` may
not be after `to`. A parameter this route does not know, a value that does not parse
(`limit=ten`), a `direction` that is neither `debit` nor `credit`, an account, identity or
asset that is not a valid identifier or symbol, and a `cursor` that is not hex are refused as
`ERR-MalformedCommand` (amendment 0032, `REQ-ER-3`), never ignored. A page may hold fewer movements than `limit` and still carry `next`: keep
passing `next` back as `cursor` until a page comes without one.

schema.description: The subject: one account, as a `did:aledgent:acct:` identifier.
Only this asset, by its symbol.
Only against this counterparty: the ledger account on the other side of the movement.

The previous page's `next`, passed back unchanged. It belongs to the request that made
it: a cursor sent with other filters is refused.
Only `debit` or `credit`; any other value is refused as `ERR-MalformedCommand`.

From this time, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch. Inclusive: a movement at exactly
this time is returned. Send it together with `to`.

The subject: one identity, as a `did:aledgent:id:` identifier. Every account of it the
caller reaches is read.

The page size, from 1 to 1000. Required: an unbounded page is refused. Any value made of
digits is a count, and one above 1000 is outside the bound (`ERR-QueryUnbounded`),
however many digits it has; a value that is not made of digits is a shape fault
(`ERR-MalformedCommand`).

Only movements on this account, which must be one of the subject's (useful when the
subject is an identity).

Up to this time, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch. Exclusive: a movement at exactly
this time is not returned. Send it together with `from`.

balances. `account`, `asset`, `from` and `to` are all required; without any of them the request
is refused as `ERR-QueryUnbounded`, and so is `from` after `to`, an `as_of` the book has not
reached, and a period of more than 1000 movements (ask for a shorter one, or page through
`movements`). A parameter this route does not know, a value that does not parse (`from=abc`)
and an `account` or `asset` that is not a valid identifier or symbol are refused as `ERR-MalformedCommand`
(amendment 0032, `REQ-ER-3`).

The asset, by its symbol. Required, as `account` is.
